> By any chance i missed urgently this element for heat pumps, that are no available for conventional heaters. It is an indicator for the ammount of ice that has accumulated in the head exchanger at the outdoor unit (ODU). If so the rpms of that fan will increase if the heat exchhange gets stuffed with ice. Would be great it this attribut can be added to the wolf SmartService integration.
> 
> ` { "ValueId": 27004700001, "SortId": 4859, "SubBundleId": 0, "ParameterId": 27004700001, "IsReadOnly": true, "NoDataPoint": false, "IsExpertProtectable": false, "Name": "Drehzahl Ventilator", "Group": "422_Einstellungen und Anzeigen", "ProtGrp": "HG <1>", "ControlType": 6, "Value": "610", "ValueState": 1, "HasDependentParameter": false, "Unit": "U/min", "Decimals": 0 },`

There is an entity providing information on the compressor level (sensor.heat_generator_1_current_capacity_specification_compressor). Not sure if ventilator is bound to this.

> [@drose28357](https://github.com/drose28357) I personally use all 3 together. You just need to make sure you don't over pull the device specially from ism7mqtt. I can use my device over wolf, ism7mqtt and this integration.

That is very interesting as everywhere i read that it was either local OR cloud solution. What are the advantages of ism7mqtt over this integration?

Ism7mqtt provides all attributes of my heat pump setup and allows to change values of some attributes. For example i can change the operation mode from auto to standby etc.
So it's is a full blown integration.

@legnad Important is that you don't open everything at the same time for a long time as the ism7 can't handle the requests and make sure you limited the parameters on the ism7mqtt. The advantage of ism7mqtt is that it's fully local and it gives you any parameter your setup has including all admin parameters. It also supports more devices and is actively supported if you provide the team with missing info.

Just as an fyi I have a new library which will support the units which you guys are looking for, but it still needs testing and implementing as it also contains other bigger changes for this integration.

As far as I can read your code changes (introducing power entity's) I missed rpm for the outdoor fan of the heat pump. The fan rpm gives an indication about the state of icing in the air heat exchanger.
br
Ditmar
P.S. thanks for your work. Waiting eagerly for 2025.3 ...
